prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
New Labour’s 1997 manifesto promises national renewal built on practicality over ideology: “what counts is what works.” It seeks a government for the many, not the few, ending old left/right dogmas, restoring trust through limited, deliverable commitments.

Core economic approach
- Stability first: low inflation (target 2.5% or less), reform the Bank of England for more independent, accountable monetary policy; borrow only to invest (“golden rule”).
- No rise in basic or top income tax rates for the Parliament; long-term goal of a 10p starting rate; cut VAT on domestic fuel to 5%; stick to existing spending limits for two years.
- Shift spending from the costs of failure to investment; encourage savings and long-term investment (new ISAs; review of corporate/capital gains taxes).
- Fund a welfare-to-work programme via a one-off windfall levy on privatised utilities.

Jobs, welfare and business
- Get 250,000 under-25s off benefit into work/training; hiring subsidies for long-term unemployed; tailored support for lone parents; crack down on benefit fraud.
- Modern labour market with minimum standards: a sensibly set national minimum wage via a Low Pay Commission; retain key 1980s union laws; recognition where a majority vote for it.
- Pro-competition reform of competition law; revive and fix PFI; support small firms (less red tape, prompt payment); create Regional Development Agencies; boost science/technology and green industries.

Public services
- Education is the top priority: smaller classes (30 or under) for ages 5–7 by ending assisted places; universal nursery for four-year-olds; literacy/numeracy drives; “setting” by ability; fresh starts for failing schools; tech in schools; strengthen teacher training and a General Teaching Council; lifelong learning (University for Industry, Individual Learning Accounts); income-contingent HE repayments.
- NHS: end the internal market; cut bureaucracy and shift funds to front-line care; treat 100,000 extra patients initially; strengthen primary care groups; longer hospital agreements; ban tobacco advertising; independent Food Standards Agency; annual real-terms funding rises.
- Crime: “tough on crime, tough on the causes.” Halve time from arrest to sentence for persistent young offenders; decentralise and strengthen CPS; consistent sentencing; more police on the beat; zero tolerance of disorder; new offences for racial harassment; drugs “czar”; free vote to ban all handguns.

Family, housing, pensions
- National childcare strategy; basic Child Benefit protected; work-life rights (limits on excessive hours, holidays, unpaid parental leave).
- Use council house receipts to build and renovate; protect tenants; tackle homelessness; fairer homebuying and mortgage protection.
- Keep the basic state pension (uprated at least with prices); retain SERPS; create “stakeholder pensions”; Royal Commission on long-term care; better support for carers.

Environment, transport, culture
- Put the environment at the heart of government; integrated transport (stronger rail regulation and a new rail authority; PPP for London Underground; better buses; safer cycling/walking); oppose 44-tonne lorries; promote clean vehicles.
- Support rural services and the Post Office; animal welfare (free vote on hunting).
- Arts, media and sport: NESTA to back young talent; reform lottery to widen access; support World Cup/Olympics bids.

Constitution and rights
- Clean up politics: end hereditary peers’ voting rights; party funding transparency and ban foreign donations; Freedom of Information Act; incorporate the ECHR into UK law.
- Devolution after referendums: a Scottish Parliament with limited tax powers; a Welsh Assembly; London mayor/authority; stronger local government and regional chambers; referendum on changing Commons voting system.

Europe, defence, world role
- Lead reform in the EU; sign the Social Chapter; euro entry only if in the national interest—subject to Cabinet, Parliament and a referendum.
- Strong defence through NATO; retain Trident; strategic defence review; push arms control and ban anti-personnel landmines.
- New Department for International Development; refocus aid on poverty reduction; aim to reverse aid cuts and work toward the 0.7% UN target; champion human rights and UN reform.
- Support the Northern Ireland peace process, human rights, fair policing and economic progress.

Five election pledges: smaller infant class sizes; fast-track persistent young offenders; cut NHS waiting lists by 100,000 via £100m in savings; get 250,000 under-25s into work funded by a windfall levy; no rise in income tax rates and cut VAT on heating to 5%, with inflation and interest rates kept as low as possible.
